Two things about it are worth knowing before a pass trusts it: it also sets the readiness gate (tolerance = (1 - screen_match) * 2304 cells, so 460 at screen_match 0.80; for comparison 59 at 0.974 and 138 at the Target default 0.94), and sc04 idles at 20 of 576 cells of animation, which is looser than the cut - masked out for screens already in the map, not for the first frame of a new one. Run run_recon.py --dry first.

Recalibrated 2026-09-07: a client update added noticeably more idle animation to the main screen. `run_recon.py --dry --screen-match N` (read-only, no model, no clicks) settled cleanly at 0.95, 0.90 and 0.80, each a short single-sample check, but real preflight runs at the old 0.974 kept failing over their full 60s settle window with bursts up to 471 of 2304 cells - past what even 0.90's tolerance (230 cells) would absorb. Set to 0.8, this codebase's own MATCH_FLOOR (see calibrate.py recut_screen_match), since the observed burst is at the edge of what that floor's tolerance (460 cells) covers and this project's own recut logic never goes looser. This is a one-off adjustment from live observation, not a full recut against real same-place/different-place transition pairs - worth re-running recut_screen_match from a real pass's transitions once one exists, to replace this with a measured value rather than a bound.
